svg.title: Four Core Seats, Six at Scaled Throughput
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-core-and-scaled-pod; chart type: org_architecture; title: Four Core Seats, Six at Scaled Throughput; subtitle: Base 1 FT + 3 C; Scaled 2 FT + 4 C; chapter number: 11; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Numeric values show the four Base seats, one per role. The Scaled model adds one full-time operations seat and one contract audit seat. Contractor counts describe people, not full-time equivalents or unlimited specialist capacity.; caption: Conservative and Base use four people; Scaled uses six. Credential-sensitive work stays with personnel qualified for that jurisdiction and service.; stages: label: Owner and client operations; value: Base one FT; Scaled two FT; numeric value: 1.0; detail: The owner controls sales, authority documents, pricing, cash collection, and client reporting. At Scaled volume, add a full-time operations lead for queue ownership and reconciliation; retain separate review of fee calculations and receipts.; label: Parcel and invoice audit delivery; value: Base one contractor; Scaled two contractors; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Audit analysts reconcile EDI and permitted API records, preserve invoice lineage, test duplicates, and prepare supported claims. The second Scaled analyst increases throughput without sharing client credentials or bypassing rate limits.; label: Utility and property specialist; value: One contractor in both operating scenarios; numeric value: 1.0; detail: A vetted specialist owns tariff interpretation, meter evidence, and property-assessment analysis within their demonstrated qualifications. Accept representation work only where this seat holds required credentials; otherwise narrow that engagement rather than inventing coverage.; label: Tax-credit documentation specialist; value: One contractor in both operating scenarios; numeric value: 1.0; detail: A qualified specialist controls WOTC prescreening timing, state certification evidence, secure records, and coordination with the employer's tax preparer. Separate administrative processing from tax-return services and maintain the required fee review.
